title: Web Development · Chapter 3
description: Style sheets (CSS): syntax, types and the cascade, selectors, combinators, pseudo-classes, typography, colours, box model, Flexbox, Grid, responsive design, preprocessors and effects.

topics.title: 3.1 CSS Basics & Syntax
topics.description: What CSS is, why it exists, rules, declaration blocks and correct syntax.

questions.prompt: What does CSS stand for?
questions.explanation: CSS = Cascading Style Sheets.

questions.prompt: What is CSS?

options.text: A simple mechanism for adding style (fonts, colours, layouts) to web documents
A protocol for transferring web pages
A database for storing website data
A language for adding content to web pages

questions.explanation: CSS adds style to HTML documents.

questions.prompt: Why was CSS introduced?

options.text: To store data on the server
To enhance the display capabilities of HTML

questions.explanation: CSS enhances how HTML is displayed. It also separates content (HTML) from presentation (CSS), so one style sheet can restyle a whole site.

questions.prompt: A rule that defines the appearance of an element on a web page is called a…
questions.explanation: A style is one rule. A style sheet is a series of rules for a page or whole site.

questions.prompt: A series of rules that defines the style for a web page or an entire web site is called a…
questions.explanation: That's a style sheet.

questions.prompt: What is a declaration block?

options.text: An HTML element that holds CSS
A list of declarations inside curly braces { }
A list of selectors separated by commas

questions.explanation: Everything between { and } is the declaration block.

questions.prompt: A declaration consists of…

options.text: A value, a colon, then a property
A property, a colon, a value, then a semicolon
A selector, a comma, then a value
A tag, an equals sign, then a value

questions.explanation: property: value;

questions.prompt: Which declaration is written correctly?
questions.explanation: Property first, then a colon, the value, and a semicolon.

questions.prompt: What is the basic CSS syntax?
questions.explanation: Selector, then a declaration block.

questions.prompt: In this CSS rule, what is part 1 (h1) called?

image.alt: The rule h1 { color: blue; } with numbered labels: 1 under h1, 2 under color, 3 under blue, and 4 above a bracket spanning the curly braces.

questions.explanation: h1 is the selector: it picks which elements to style.

questions.prompt: In this CSS rule, what is part 2 (color) called?

image.alt: The rule h1 { color: blue; } with numbered labels: 1 under h1, 2 under color, 3 under blue, and 4 above a bracket spanning the curly braces.

questions.explanation: color is the property; blue is its value; everything in { } is the declaration block.

questions.prompt: In this CSS rule, what is part 4 (everything between the braces) called?

image.alt: The rule h1 { color: blue; } with numbered labels: 1 under h1, 2 under color, 3 under blue, and 4 above a bracket spanning the curly braces.

questions.explanation: The declaration block holds one or more declarations.

questions.prompt: Which is a valid CSS comment?
questions.explanation: CSS only has /* … */ comments. <!-- --> is HTML.

questions.prompt: Which property sets the TEXT colour of an element?
questions.explanation: It's simply color. Your notes' example `fontcolor: navy` isn't a real property — the browser would ignore it.

questions.prompt: If you misspell a property, like `font-szie: 12px;`, the browser simply ignores that declaration.
questions.explanation: Browsers skip declarations they don't understand and keep reading the rest. (font-szie in your notes is a typo for font-size.)

questions.prompt: `font-size: 14 pt;` (with a space between the number and unit) is valid CSS.
questions.explanation: There must be no space between a number and its unit: 14pt. With the space, the declaration is ignored.

topics.title: 3.2 Types of CSS & the Cascade
topics.description: Inline, embedded and external CSS, which overrides which, plus specificity, !important and inheritance.

questions.prompt: What are the 3 types of CSS? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Inline, embedded/internal, and external/linked.

questions.prompt: Which type of CSS controls the style for a SINGLE web page?
questions.explanation: Embedded CSS lives in <style> tags inside that page's <head>.

questions.prompt: Which type of CSS defines a style for only a SINGLE HTML tag?
questions.explanation: Inline CSS uses the style attribute on one tag.

questions.prompt: Which type of CSS controls the appearance of MULTIPLE pages in a website?
questions.explanation: One external .css file can be linked from every page.

questions.prompt: Which type of CSS is this?
questions.explanation: The style attribute sits directly on the tag, so only this <h1> is affected.

questions.prompt: Which type of CSS does this line add?
questions.explanation: <link> in <head> connects an external style sheet.

questions.prompt: For embedded CSS, where do you put the <style> … </style> tags?
questions.explanation: Embedded CSS goes in <style> inside <head>.

questions.prompt: Which statements about EXTERNAL style sheets are true? (select all that apply)

options.text: They are applied with a <link> in the <head>
They are a separate text file (e.g. style.css)
They help every page use a consistent style
They are written inside the style attribute

questions.explanation: The last option describes inline CSS.

questions.prompt: In <link rel="______" href="style.css">, what value goes in rel?
questions.explanation: rel="stylesheet" tells the browser the linked file is CSS.

questions.prompt: According to your notes, which type of CSS has the HIGHEST priority?
questions.explanation: Inline overrides embedded and external.

questions.prompt: According to your notes, which order is correct (highest priority first)?
questions.explanation: Inline beats embedded, which beats external. Strictly, embedded vs external is decided by ORDER: whichever comes later in the <head> wins. Embedded <style> is usually placed after the <link>, so it wins.

questions.prompt: What does “cascading” mean in Cascading Style Sheets?

options.text: Styles can only flow from parent to child
Several rules can apply to one element, and the browser has rules to decide which one wins
CSS files load one after another slowly
Style sheets must be stacked in folders

questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. Conflicts are settled by importance (!important), then specificity, then source order (later wins).

questions.prompt: Three rules target the same <h1 id="title" class="heading">. Which colour wins?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. Specificity: ID > class/attribute/pseudo-class > element. So #title wins regardless of order.

questions.prompt: Two rules have exactly the same specificity. Which one is applied?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. With equal specificity, source order decides: the later rule wins.

questions.prompt: What does !important do in `color: red !important;`?

options.text: Makes this declaration override normal declarations, even those with higher specificity
Marks the line as a comment

questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. It beats normal rules (even inline styles). Use it sparingly — it makes CSS hard to maintain.

questions.prompt: Properties like color and font-family are inherited by child elements, but border and margin are not.
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. Text-related properties inherit; box properties (border, margin, padding, background) don't.

topics.title: 3.3 Selectors
topics.description: Tag, class, ID, grouping, universal, the five selector categories and attribute selectors.

questions.prompt: Which selector types are listed in your notes? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Tag, class and advanced (IDs, pseudo-classes).

questions.prompt: A TAG selector like `body { … }` does what?

options.text: Styles elements with a matching class
Redefines the look of every element of that tag
Styles one element with a matching id

questions.explanation: Tag selectors target all elements of that type.

questions.prompt: A class selector always begins with…
questions.explanation: .indent { … }

questions.prompt: An ID selector begins with…
questions.explanation: #myID { … }

questions.prompt: Write the selector for elements with class="indent".
questions.explanation: Classes start with a dot.

questions.prompt: Write the selector for the element with id="myID".
questions.explanation: IDs start with #.

questions.prompt: Which elements does `p.beginning { … }` style?

options.text: elements inside an element with class beginning

questions.explanation:
Tag + class (no space) = only that tag with that class. `.beginning` alone would target both

and

.

questions.prompt:
Which selector styles BOTH

and

?
questions.explanation: A class selector on its own matches any tag.

questions.prompt: According to your notes, class selectors can only be defined in embedded and external style sheets (not inline).
questions.explanation: Inline styles sit on one tag, so there's no selector. Classes are defined in <style> or a .css file and used with class="…".

questions.prompt: Which selector matches ALL elements on the page?
questions.explanation: * is the universal selector. (Your notes list `*` under “single element type” — the labels look shifted: `*` = all elements, `p` = a single element type, `h1, h2, h3` = multiple types.)

questions.prompt: What does the comma do in `h1, h2, h3 { background-color: purple; }`?

options.text: Groups selectors: the same style applies to h1, h2 AND h3
Selects h3 inside h2 inside h1

questions.explanation: A comma-separated list groups selectors that share the same declarations.

questions.prompt: Which elements does `#p1, #p3 { background-color: aqua; }` style?

options.text: The elements with id="p1" and id="p3"

questions.explanation: A grouped list of ID selectors.

questions.prompt: Which are the five categories of CSS selectors? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: The five categories from your notes.

questions.prompt: Which category selects elements based on a certain STATE (e.g. being hovered)?
questions.explanation: :hover, :visited, :focus are pseudo-classes.

questions.prompt: Which category selects and styles a PART of an element (e.g. its first letter)?
questions.explanation: ::first-letter, ::before are pseudo-elements.

questions.prompt: Which category selects elements based on the RELATIONSHIP between them?
questions.explanation: Combinators: descendant (space), child (>), adjacent sibling (+), general sibling (~).

questions.prompt: Which elements does this selector match?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. [attribute="value"] is an attribute selector.

questions.prompt: What does `a[href^="https"]` select?

options.text: Links whose href CONTAINS https anywhere
Links whose href STARTS with https
Links whose href ENDS with https

questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. ^= starts with, $= ends with (e.g. a[href$=".pdf"]), *= contains.

questions.prompt: What does `.btn.primary` (no space) select?

options.text: Nothing — two classes can't be combined
Elements with class primary inside a .btn
Elements that have BOTH classes, e.g. class="btn primary"

questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. Chained classes = same element. With a space (.btn .primary) it means a descendant.

topics.title: 3.1 Combinators
topics.description: Extra detail — descendant (space), child (>), adjacent sibling (+) and general sibling (~).

questions.prompt: What does the space in `div p` mean?

options.text:
Only

elements that are direct children of a

Any

inside a

, at any depth (descendant)

questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. The space is the descendant combinator.

questions.prompt: What does `ul > li` select?

options.text: <li> elements that are DIRECT children of a <ul>

questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. > is the child combinator: one level down only.

questions.prompt: Which symbol is the CHILD combinator?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. div > p.

questions.prompt: What does `h2 + p` select?

options.text:
The first

that comes immediately after an

(same parent)

questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. + is the adjacent sibling combinator.

questions.prompt: What does `h2 ~ p` select?

options.text:
All

siblings that come after an

questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. ~ is the general sibling combinator.

questions.prompt: With this HTML, which paragraphs does `div p` style? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. Descendant = any depth inside the div, so A and B. C is outside the div.

questions.prompt: With the same HTML, which paragraphs does `div > p` style? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. Only A is a direct child of the div. B's parent is <section>.

questions.prompt: With the same HTML, which paragraph does `div + p` style? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. C is the element immediately after the , at the same level.

topics.title: 3.3 Pseudo-classes & Pseudo-elements
topics.description: Link states, :hover, :focus, structural pseudo-classes, ::before/::after and more.

questions.prompt: Which pseudo-class styles links the user has NOT visited yet?
questions.explanation: :link = unvisited.

questions.prompt: With this CSS, a link the user has already opened appears in which colour?
questions.explanation: :visited applies to links already visited.

questions.prompt: When does `a:active` apply?

options.text: While the link is being clicked (pressed)
After the link has been visited
When the mouse is over it

questions.explanation: :active = at the moment of clicking.

questions.prompt: Which pseudo-class applies when the mouse pointer is OVER an element?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. :hover. Phones have no hover, so don't hide important things behind it.

questions.prompt: What is the correct order for link pseudo-classes in your CSS?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. “LoVe HAte” (LVHA). They have equal specificity, so later rules win; in this order hover and active can override link/visited.

questions.prompt: Which pseudo-class applies when an input is selected/clicked into, ready for typing?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. input:focus { outline: 2px solid blue; }.

questions.prompt: Which selector styles the FIRST <li> in each list?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. :first-child and :last-child.

questions.prompt: Write the pseudo-class to stripe every ODD table row: tr:______
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. tr:nth-child(odd) or tr:nth-child(2n+1). Even rows: nth-child(even) or nth-child(2n).

questions.prompt: Which items does `li:nth-child(3)` select?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. A plain number picks that one position. Every third would be :nth-child(3n).

questions.prompt: What does `button:not(.primary)` select?

options.text: Buttons that do NOT have the class primary

questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. :not() excludes matches.

questions.prompt: Which pseudo-classes describe the state of FORM inputs? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. ::first-letter is a pseudo-element for text.

questions.prompt: Which uses double colons (::) in modern CSS?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. One colon = pseudo-class (a state). Two colons = pseudo-element (a part). Browsers still accept old single-colon :before.

questions.prompt: What do ::before and ::after do?

options.text: Run JavaScript before or after loading
Style links before and after visiting
Select the element before or after
Insert generated content before or after an element's content

questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. They need a content property, e.g. .new::after { content: " 🔥"; }.

questions.prompt: `p::before { color: red; }` with no content property will show something on the page.
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. Without `content` (even content: ""), ::before/::after aren't created.

questions.prompt: Which pseudo-element makes a large “drop cap” first letter of a paragraph?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. ::first-letter styles the first letter; ::first-line the first line.

questions.prompt: Which pseudo-element styles text the user highlights with the mouse?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. ::selection. Related: ::placeholder styles input hint text, ::marker styles list bullets/numbers.

topics.title: 3.2 Typography & Text Styling
topics.description: font-family, sizes and units, weight, style, alignment, decoration, spacing and shadows.

questions.prompt: Why does this rule list several fonts?
questions.code: h1 { font-family: Georgia, "Times New Roman", Times, serif; }

options.text: The browser mixes all four fonts together
Each word uses the next font in the list
They are fallbacks: the browser uses the first font available on the device
Only the last font is used

questions.explanation: If Georgia isn't installed, the browser tries Times New Roman, then Times, then any serif font.

questions.prompt: Font names that contain spaces, like "Times New Roman", should be wrapped in quotes.
questions.explanation: Quote multi-word font names. Generic family names (serif, sans-serif) are never quoted.

questions.prompt: Which are GENERIC font families you can put last as a final fallback? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. Arial is a specific font; bold is a weight.

questions.prompt: Which property changes the size of text?
questions.explanation: e.g. font-size: 32px;

questions.prompt: The `rem` unit is relative to…
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. 1rem = root font size (usually 16px). `em` (for font-size) is relative to the PARENT's font size, so nested ems multiply.

questions.prompt: A parent has font-size: 20px. Its child has font-size: 1.5em. What is the child's font size?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. 1.5 × 20px = 30px.

questions.prompt: Which unit is mainly intended for PRINT (like in Word documents)?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. pt is a print unit (1pt = 1/72 inch). On screens px, em and rem are more common. Your notes use pt in `text-indent: 8pt`.

questions.prompt: Which numeric font-weight is the same as bold?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. 400 = normal, 700 = bold. Values run from 100 (thin) to 900 (black).

questions.prompt: Which declaration makes text italic?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. font-style: italic | normal | oblique.

questions.prompt: Which value of text-align spreads lines so both left and right edges are straight?
questions.explanation: text-align: left | right | center | justify. Your notes use text-align: center on h1.

questions.prompt: How do you remove the underline from links?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. text-decoration also takes underline, overline and line-through.

questions.prompt: Which property turns text into CAPITAL letters without changing the HTML?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. text-transform: uppercase | lowercase | capitalize.

questions.prompt: What does `p { text-indent: 8pt; }` (from your notes) do?

options.text: Indents the FIRST line of each paragraph by 8pt

questions.explanation: text-indent affects the first line only.

questions.prompt: Which property controls the space BETWEEN LINES of text?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. line-height: 1.5 is a common readable value.

questions.prompt: Which property controls the space between individual CHARACTERS?
questions.explanation: Your notes show `letter-spacing: 1em` (they missed the colon). word-spacing is the gap between words.

questions.prompt: In `text-shadow: 2px 2px 4px gray;`, what is 4px?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. Order: x-offset, y-offset, blur, colour.

questions.prompt: How can you use a custom font that isn't installed on users' devices?

options.text: Load it with @font-face (or a font service link such as Google Fonts)

questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. @font-face { font-family: "MyFont"; src: url(myfont.woff2); } then use font-family: "MyFont".

topics.title: 3.3 Colours, Backgrounds & Images
topics.description: Colour formats, background properties, gradients and image fitting.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between `color` and `background-color`?

options.text: color sets the text colour; background-color fills behind the element

questions.explanation: e.g. body { background-color: linen; } h1 { color: maroon; }

questions.prompt: Which are valid ways to write a colour in CSS? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. Names, hex, rgb()/rgba() and hsl()/hsla() are all valid.

questions.prompt: Which colour is #000000?
questions.explanation: Hex is #RRGGBB. All zeros = no light = black. Your notes use it for the body background.

questions.prompt: Write the hex code for white.
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. #FFFFFF (or the shorthand #FFF).

questions.prompt: Which colour is #FF0000?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. RR = FF (full red), GG = 00, BB = 00.

questions.prompt: The shorthand hex #f80 is the same as…
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. Each digit is doubled: f→ff, 8→88, 0→00.

questions.prompt: In `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5)`, what does 0.5 control?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. Alpha goes from 0 (invisible) to 1 (solid).

questions.prompt: In `hsl(120, 100%, 50%)`, what does 120 represent?

options.text: Hue — an angle on the colour wheel (120 = green)

questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. hsl = hue (0–360°), saturation (%), lightness (%).

questions.prompt: What is the difference between `opacity: 0.5` and `background-color: rgba(0,0,0,0.5)`?

options.text: opacity fades the WHOLE element including its text; rgba only makes the background see-through

questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. Use rgba/hsla when you want readable solid text on a see-through background.

questions.prompt: Which declaration sets an image as a background?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. background-image takes url(…).

questions.prompt: By default a small background image is…
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. Use background-repeat: no-repeat to show it once.

questions.prompt: Which background-size value makes the image cover the whole element, cropping if needed?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. cover fills and may crop; contain shows the whole image and may leave gaps.

questions.prompt: What does `background-attachment: fixed;` do?

options.text: The background stays still while the page scrolls
The background is attached to the mouse

questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. This creates a simple parallax effect.

questions.prompt: Which line creates a background fading from red on the left to blue on the right?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. Gradients are images, so they go in background-image (or background). radial-gradient makes a circular one.

questions.prompt: What is the `background` property?

options.text: A shorthand that sets several background properties at once
A property that only works on <body>

questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. e.g. background: #000 url("star.png") no-repeat center;

questions.prompt: An must fill a 300×300 box without stretching or squashing. Which declaration?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. object-fit is for /

topics.title: Box Model, Display & Positioning
topics.description: Extra — the box model, margin/padding shorthand, box-sizing, display, position, z-index, overflow, float.

questions.prompt: What is the missing layer marked “?” in the CSS box model?

image.alt: Nested boxes: the outermost dashed area is labelled Margin, then a dark Border, then a light area marked with a question mark, then the Content box in the centre.

questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. From inside out: content → padding → border → margin.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between padding and margin?

options.text: Padding is outside; margin is inside
Padding is space INSIDE the border; margin is space OUTSIDE the border

questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. Background colour shows through padding but not through margin.

questions.prompt: In `margin: 10px 20px 30px 40px;`, which side gets 40px?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. Clockwise from the top: top, right, bottom, left (remember “TRouBLe”).

questions.prompt: `padding: 10px 20px;` gives…

options.text: 10px left and right, 20px top and bottom
10px top and bottom, 20px left and right

questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. Two values = vertical, horizontal.

questions.prompt: How do you centre a block element with a set width horizontally?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. Auto left and right margins share the free space equally. (text-align centres inline content inside a block.)

questions.prompt: With the default box-sizing (content-box), what is the total width of this box in px?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. 200 content + 20+20 padding + 5+5 border = 250px. With box-sizing: border-box it would stay 200px.

questions.prompt: What does `box-sizing: border-box;` change?

options.text: It adds a border to every box
width/height now include padding and border, so the box stays the size you set

questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. Many developers set * { box-sizing: border-box; } so sizes are predictable.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between `display: none` and `visibility: hidden`?

options.text: display: none only works on images
display: none removes the element and its space; visibility: hidden hides it but keeps the space

questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. Hidden elements still take up room; display:none elements are gone from the layout.

questions.prompt: Which display value lets elements sit side by side in a line BUT still accept width and height?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. inline ignores width/height; block takes the full line; inline-block is in between.

questions.prompt: Which position value places an element relative to the browser window, so it stays put when scrolling (e.g. a chat button)?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. fixed = relative to the viewport.

questions.prompt: An element with `position: absolute;` is positioned relative to…

options.text: Its nearest positioned ancestor (one with position other than static)

questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. That's why parents often get position: relative. If no ancestor is positioned, it uses the page.

questions.prompt: What does `position: relative; top: 10px;` do?

options.text: Moves it 10px from the top of the page
Moves the element 10px down from where it would normally be, leaving its original space

questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. relative shifts the element visually; other elements act as if it hadn't moved.

questions.prompt: Which position value makes a header scroll normally and then STICK to the top once it reaches it?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. position: sticky; top: 0;

questions.prompt: What does z-index control?

options.text: Which positioned element appears on top when they overlap

questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. Higher z-index = closer to the viewer. It needs a position (other than static), or a flex/grid item.

questions.prompt: Content is too tall for its box. Which declaration adds a scrollbar only when needed?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. visible (default) spills out, hidden clips, scroll always shows bars, auto shows them when needed.

questions.prompt: What does `float: left;` on an image do?

options.text: Moves the image to the left and lets text wrap around its right side
Makes the image hover over the page

questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. Use clear: both on a later element to stop wrapping. Flexbox/grid have replaced floats for layout.

questions.prompt: Which declaration makes a square image into a circle?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. border-radius rounds corners; 50% on a square gives a circle.

questions.prompt: In `border: 2px solid red;`, which part is the border STYLE?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. Shorthand order: width, style (solid/dashed/dotted/double), colour.

topics.title: 3.4 Flexbox
topics.description: Covers a section missing from your notes. display: flex, main/cross axis, justify-content, align-items, wrap, gap and flex item properties.

questions.prompt: Which declaration turns an element into a flex container?
questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. display: flex on the PARENT; its direct children become flex items.

questions.prompt: `display: flex` is set on the container, and it arranges the container's direct children.
questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. Grandchildren are not affected unless their own parent is also a flex container.

questions.prompt: Flexbox is a one-dimensional layout system (it lays items out in a row OR a column).
questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. Grid is two-dimensional (rows AND columns).

questions.prompt: What is the default flex-direction?
questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. Items line up left to right in a row by default.

questions.prompt: This container uses flex-direction: column. Which arrow shows the MAIN axis?

image.alt: A flex container with three items stacked vertically and the label flex-direction: column. Arrow A points downwards beside the items; arrow B points to the right underneath.

options.text: Arrow A (vertical, the direction items flow)

questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. The main axis follows flex-direction. With column it's vertical; the cross axis is horizontal.

questions.prompt: justify-content aligns flex items along the…
questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. justify-content → main axis; align-items → cross axis.

questions.prompt: Which diagram shows `justify-content: space-between`?

questions.prompt: Which three declarations perfectly centre a child both horizontally and vertically?

display: flex; align-content: middle; justify-items: center;
display: block; text-align: center; vertical-align: middle;

questions.prompt: What is the default value of align-items?
questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. Items stretch to fill the container's cross size unless they have a fixed height. (The initial value is `normal`, which behaves like stretch for flex items.)

questions.prompt: Items squeeze onto one line and overflow. Which declaration lets them move onto new lines?

options.text: They grow to share the available space equally

questions.prompt: The `flex` shorthand `flex: 2 1 200px;` sets which three properties, in order?

options.text: The item's starting size before free space is shared out

questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. Think of it as the item's ideal width (in a row).

questions.prompt: Which property moves one flex item to a different visual position without changing the HTML?
questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. Default order is 0; lower numbers come first. (Screen readers still follow the HTML order.)

questions.prompt: Which property overrides align-items for ONE particular item?
questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. e.g. .logo { align-self: flex-start; }

questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. column-reverse stacks bottom to top.

topics.title: 3.4 CSS Grid
topics.description: Covers a section missing from your notes. display: grid, columns/rows, fr, repeat(), minmax(), gap, spanning, line numbers and areas.

questions.prompt: Which declaration turns an element into a grid container?
questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. display: grid on the parent.

questions.prompt: How is Grid different from Flexbox?

options.text: Flexbox is newer and replaces Grid
Grid is two-dimensional (rows and columns); Flexbox is one-dimensional (a row or a column)

questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. Use Grid for page layouts and card grids; Flexbox for a row of buttons or a navbar.

questions.prompt: What does `grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr;` create?
questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. fr = a fraction of the free space.

questions.prompt: What does the fr unit mean?

options.text: A fraction of the available free space

questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. 1fr 2fr → the second column is twice as wide.

questions.prompt: `grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 1fr);` is the same as…
questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. repeat(count, size) saves typing.

questions.prompt: What does `grid-template-columns: 250px 1fr;` create?

options.text: A fixed 250px column (e.g. sidebar) and a second column that takes the rest

questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. Mixing fixed and flexible sizes is very common.

questions.prompt: Which grid-column value makes Item 1 span the first two columns, as shown?

image.alt: A three-column grid with lines numbered 1 to 4 across the top. Item 1 covers columns one and two (from line 1 to line 3); Item 2 is in column three; Items 3, 4 and 5 fill the second row.

questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. Grid LINES are numbered from 1. Item 1 starts at line 1 and ends at line 3. `grid-column: span 2;` also works.

questions.prompt: A grid has 3 columns. How many vertical grid LINES does it have?
questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. n columns have n + 1 lines.

questions.prompt: What does `grid-row: span 2;` do to an item?
questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. span counts tracks instead of naming lines.

questions.prompt: Which property sets the space between grid rows and columns?
questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. gap (or row-gap / column-gap).

questions.prompt: What is `minmax(200px, 1fr)` for?

questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. It sets minimum and maximum sizes.

questions.prompt: What does this create?

options.text: As many 200px-minimum columns as fit, automatically wrapping on smaller screens (responsive without media queries)

questions.prompt: How does this layout work?

options.text: It sets fonts for each area
It names areas so each element can be placed with grid-area (header on top, sidebar + main, footer at the bottom)
It creates text labels on the page

questions.prompt: Which single declaration centres every item inside its grid cell, both ways?

questions.prompt: You need a whole-page layout with header, sidebar, content and footer. Which is usually the better fit?
questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. Grid handles rows and columns together. Flexbox is great inside each part (e.g. the nav links).

topics.title: 3.5 Responsive Design & Media Queries
topics.description: Covers a section missing from your notes. Viewport, media queries, breakpoints, mobile-first, fluid units and responsive images.

questions.prompt: What is responsive web design?

options.text: Designing pages that adapt their layout to different screen sizes and devices
Pages that reply to user messages

questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. One site that works on phones, tablets and desktops.

questions.prompt: What happens on a phone if the page has NO viewport meta tag?

options.text: The phone pretends to be a wide desktop screen (~980px) and shrinks the page, so text looks tiny

questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. Always include <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">.

questions.prompt: Which CSS at-rule starts a media query?
questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. @media (max-width: 600px) { … }

questions.prompt: When do the styles inside this media query apply?

options.text: When the viewport is wider than 600px
When the viewport is 600px wide or narrower

questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. max-width = “up to”. min-width = “from this width and up”.

questions.prompt: With this CSS, how many columns does .grid have on a 500px-wide phone?
questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. 500px is below 768px, so the media query doesn't apply: 1 column.

questions.prompt: With the same CSS, how many columns on a 1024px-wide laptop?
questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. 1024px ≥ 768px, so the min-width query applies: 2 columns.

questions.prompt: The CSS above is an example of which approach?

options.text: Desktop-first: base styles for desktops, max-width queries for phones
Mobile-first: base styles for small screens, min-width queries add features for bigger screens

questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. Mobile-first uses min-width; desktop-first uses max-width.

questions.prompt: What is a breakpoint?

options.text: A screen width at which the layout changes
A pause in a CSS animation
Where a line of text wraps

questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. e.g. 600px, 768px, 1024px — chosen where your design starts to look cramped.

questions.prompt: Which are real media features you can test in a media query? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. Media features describe the device or user settings.

questions.prompt: Which media query applies only when the page is PRINTED?
questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. Media types: screen, print, all. You can hide the nav and ads when printing.

questions.prompt: How do you apply styles only between 600px and 900px wide?
questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. Join conditions with and.

questions.prompt: What is 1vw?
questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. vw/vh are viewport units: 100vh = full screen height.

questions.prompt: How wide is an element with width: 50vw on a 400px-wide phone? (in px)
questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. 50% of 400px = 200px.

questions.prompt: Which CSS makes images shrink to fit small screens without distortion?
questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. max-width stops overflow; height: auto keeps the proportions.

questions.prompt: What do the srcset attribute and the <picture> element help with?

options.text: Serving different image files for different screen sizes/resolutions

questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. Phones can download a smaller image, saving data.

questions.prompt: What does `font-size: clamp(1rem, 4vw, 2rem);` do?

Clamps the element to the top of the page

questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. clamp(min, preferred, max) gives fluid typography.

They scale with the screen or user's font settings

questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. Fluid sizes adapt; fixed widths cause horizontal scrolling on small screens.

topics.title: 3.6 CSS Preprocessors (Sass / LESS)

questions.prompt: What is a CSS preprocessor?

A language that extends CSS with features like variables and nesting, then compiles into normal CSS
A browser plug-in that reads CSS faster

questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. Syntactically Awesome Style Sheets.

questions.prompt: What does LESS stand for?
questions.explanation: Covers a section missing from your notes. LESS = Leaner Style Sheets.

options.text: Running in the browser without compiling
